narrative.overview: Patchwork treats multi-team issue tracking as a high-density operational dispatch board rather than a decorative marketing wall. Inspired by Swiss railway timetables and architectural drafting sheets, every pixel serves scannability: a dark cobalt-slate left navigation rail anchors the Org -> Team -> Project -> Board hierarchy, while the warm drafting-paper canvas holds crisp 1px-bordered columns, tabular ticket keys, and a slide-over detail inspector.
keyCharacteristics: High-signal operational density with 12px base workspace copy and tabular-nums alignment on all ticket keys, counts, and WIP gauges.
Tonal architectural contrast pairing a deep slate navigation rail (#141920) with a low-glare warm stone workspace ground (#F6F5F2).
Precision WIP capacity bars integrated directly into Kanban column headers to surface bottlenecks before cards overflow.

rules.name: The Structural Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every workspace boundary—navigation rail, top breadcrumb bar, Kanban column, and ticket card—is separated by a 1px structural border (#D8D6D0 / #222A35) rather than heavy drop shadows.

rules.name: The Tabular Telemetry Rule
rules.body: Every ticket key, WIP ratio (2/4), attachment byte size, and timestamp must enforce font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so vertical columns scan without jitter.

dos: Do keep ticket cards compact (p-2.5) with monospace keys (TELE-1) and priority badges on the top row.
Do use tabular-nums on all ticket numbers, WIP counters, and file sizes.
Do maintain >=4.5:1 contrast on all secondary slate labels in both light and dark modes.
donts: Don't place uppercase eyebrow/kicker labels above section headings.
Don't use decorative glassmorphism, gradient text, or >1px colored side borders on ticket cards.
Don't use emoji or raw Unicode symbols in place of SVG icons.
